scope: Pinned primary-source investigation and candidate owned fixture environment change. This is not a proven root cause or an executed Mac repair.

established: C/Swift importer compilation, real CSSM partition ADD, exact four partition readback and fresh-process challenge all succeeded in the prior Mac run.
The first framework codesign invocation still exited 1 with item-not-found. Actual codeSign policy evaluation with the explicit owned root exited 0; the ordinary valid identity list was empty.
notEstablished: No new Mac execution by this work.
Matching1/valid0 alone does not establish the precise modern CLI call that failed.
No evidence that the target CMS signing path reconstructed the identity with a NULL keychain.

primaryFacts.conclusion: Historical public CLI selects from the supplied keychain with code-sign policy, false valid-only filtering and exact certificate SHA1. Its identity preference check precedes this search.

Historical CLI reports global identity/prepare failures without a target path, while per-target failures include it. Observed unprefixed stderr is compatible with an early stage; it does not prove the current binary call site.
SecIdentityCreateWithCertificate searches the explicit keychain list, or the default list if NULL.
Identity reconstruction binds a private key by the certificate public-key hash with the selected keychain search scope.
One current SecurityTool helper scopes identity enumeration but then queries private-key attributes without carrying that list. No proof that the current codesign executable calls this helper.
security find-identity performs distinct matching and valid-only policy searches; the output lists describe different checks.
The library pre-signing context uses the supplied identity certificate; failed trust evaluation is logged as nonfatal here.
The CMS encoder receives the selected SecIdentity and creates signer info from it.
Signer creation copies the private key from the supplied identity and checks that its class is private; this is not default-keychain reconstruction.
Trust constraints may be policy-limited. An empty array is broad trust, not absence; trustRoot is restricted to a self-signed root.
User trust modification can require GUI authentication. This implementation does not claim that an earlier no-interaction authorization preflight guarantees no later OS authorization request.
CopyTrustSettings missing exact certificate is errSecItemNotFound. Set replaces that certificate settings; Remove targets the exact certificate/domain.
The public trust writer internally creates an authorization reference and permits interaction. The caller cannot pass a no-interaction flag to Set/Remove.

Public settings readback reconstructs the SecPolicy and can include generated descriptive policyName. Validate the policy OID and explicit trust result; do not mistake that metadata for a broader constraint.
The user trust authorization right is com.apple.trust-settings.user; the code requests it through public Authorization APIs without changing authorization rules.
SecPolicyCreateWithProperties is the public nullable policy constructor used by the candidate; no private code-sign policy constructor is imported.

currentDocumentation.conclusion: Current documentation describes trust-chain, validity and code-sign purpose checks in identity selection. --keychain restricts the identity search file. A separate explicit-anchor verify-cert invocation does not set that CLI environment.

currentDocumentation.section: Check for an expired certificate; Check for a missing issuer
currentDocumentation.conclusion: Apple DTS shows an unprefixed item-not-found for an expired identity, and explains that untrusted identity symptoms have multiple causes. This supports investigating policy filtering without treating the observed error as proof of a missing key.

currentDocumentation.section: Test from Terminal; Working without the GUI
currentDocumentation.conclusion: Apple DTS distinguishes trusted identity availability, keychain unlocking and private-key ACL access. These are independent prerequisites.

sourceVersionBoundary.warning: Neither pinned source set is asserted to match the exact current hosted codesign executable. The OSS repository import dates are not platform release dates.

candidateChange.purpose: Give only this disposable hosted Mac fixture its own exact synthetic certificate as a temporary user-domain codeSign trustRoot; keep actual platform codesign and independent CMS/MachO verification mandatory.
candidateChange.processWideMutation: This intentionally changes per-user trust during the test; it is not represented as an unchanged global user environment.
gates: Only Darwin + GITHUB_ACTIONS=true + RUNNER_ENVIRONMENT=github-hosted + RUNNER_OS=macOS in both producer and importer.
Exact certificate user settings must be absent; no existing entry, including an empty broad-trust array, is overwritten.

Public AuthorizationCopyRights has no InteractionAllowed flag and must succeed before each actual mutation. Public Set/Remove can still request system authorization; no credentials, clicks, sudo or user responses are supplied.
Set/Remove execute in the existing bounded private-input child process. A deadline, rejection or nonzero exit remains failure.
Read back a single actual codeSign policy plus explicit trustRoot result; no allowed errors/app policy/broad trust accepted.
Actual security find-identity -v must show exact SHA1 0 before, 1 after install, and 0 after removal.
Mark cleanup intent before starting Set so a committed write with a lost ACK is still cleaned in finally.
Remove only the exact certificate with the expected bounded policy, then actually read missing. Preserve primary and cleanup failures independently; cleanup failure keeps the whole stage failed.
noChange: No other certificate import or trust rewrite.
No sudo, authorization database edits, different signing backend, ad-hoc target signatures, relaxed CMS or MachO verification.
limits: Actual headless authorization availability and signing success remain unverified until a new finite Mac run.
SIGKILL can bypass parent finally; the host must be disposable. Child termination can leave an uncertain OS mutation; a failed run never earns a successful manifest.
Cleanup proof means the exact certificate was absent at the actual final read, not a universal assertion about all system state or future OS work.
